proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(U_0=\operatorname{col}(\Lambda)\) and \(V_0=\operatorname{col}(F)\).  The loading and factor Gram envelopes imply that both spaces have dimension \(r\) and
\[
s_r\!\left(\frac{\Lambda F^{\top}}{\sigma\sqrt T}\right)
\geq
\frac{\sqrt{N\underline\lambda}\sqrt{T\underline f}}
{\overline\sigma\sqrt T}
\geq C_0\sqrt m,
\qquad
C_0=\frac{\sqrt{\underline\lambda\underline f}}{\overline\sigma}>0. \tag{1}
\]
All bounds below are uniform when \((\eta,h)\) ranges over a fixed compact subset of
\(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times[-\overline h,\overline h]\).

The share envelope and finite supported-variance envelope make the following vectors well defined:
\[
e_1=\frac d{\sqrt{n_1}},\qquad
e_2=\frac{a_S-\mu_{a,N}d}{\sqrt{n_1v_{a,N}}},\qquad
f_1=\frac{qvec}{\sqrt{t_1}},\qquad
f_2=\frac{b_S-\mu_{b,T}qvec}{\sqrt{t_1v_{b,T}}}. \tag{2}
\]
The definitions of the supported means and variances show directly that each pair is orthonormal.  The four exact orthogonality assumptions give
\(e_1,e_2\in U_0^\perp\) and \(f_1,f_2\in V_0^\perp\).  For
\(\beta=\gamma+\sigma x/\sqrt m\), define
\[
P_x=\frac{H-(\beta-\gamma)D}{\sigma\sqrt T}.
\]
For every fixed \(M\), the noise-scale bound gives
\(\sup_{|x|\leq M}|\sigma x|/\sqrt m\leq\overline\sigma M/\sqrt m<\varepsilon\)
for all sufficiently large panels.  The coefficient-domain assumption therefore ensures that every such \(\beta\) belongs to the interior of \(\mathcal B\); no boundary minimizer is introduced on the compact local coordinate set.
Substitution of \(H=\theta a_Sb_S^{\top}/\sqrt m\), \(D=dqvec^{\top}\), and (2) yields the exact identity
\[
P_x=(e_1,e_2)B_{NT,h}(x)(f_1,f_2)^{\top}. \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, the scalar multiplying the heterogeneous component is
\[
\frac{\theta\sqrt{n_1t_1}}{\sigma\sqrt{mT}}
=h\sqrt{\frac Nm}\sqrt{p_Nq_T}=h\kappa_{NT},
\]
and the scalar multiplying the coefficient displacement is \(x\kappa_{NT}\).  This proves the stated rectangular normalization without an approximation.

Complete orthonormal bases beginning with bases of \(U_0\) and \(V_0\).  Gaussian orthogonal invariance and (3) give
\[
\frac{Y-\beta D}{\sigma\sqrt T}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
G+Z_{11}&Z_{12}\\
Z_{21}&Z_{22}+P_x
\end{pmatrix}, \tag{4}
\]
where \(s_r(G)\geq C_0\sqrt m\), the entries of \(Z\) are independent
\(\mathcal N(0,1/T)\), and the nonzero part of \(P_x\) has the two-by-two representation (3).  The cited rectangular Gaussian outlier theorem at zero perturbation gives
\(\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_p(1)\).  The lower block equations for a singular pair associated with one of the first \(r\) singular values in (4), together with (1), therefore imply that both lower singular-vector blocks have norm \(O_p(m^{-1/2})\), uniformly for \(|x|\leq M\).

Interpolate linearly from \(P_0\) to \(P_x\).  At a differentiability point, the derivative of the sum of the first \(r\) squared singular values is twice the Frobenius inner product of the perturbation with the lower-right block of the corresponding rank-\(r\) truncated singular expansion.  The preceding two lower-block bounds and the \(O_p(\sqrt m)\) strong singular values make that block \(O_p(m^{-1/2})\).  The variational characterization of the sum of the first \(r\) squared singular values makes it locally Lipschitz, so integration, with one-sided derivatives at the finitely many crossings, gives
\[
\sup_{|x|\leq M}\left|
\sum_{j=1}^r s_j(G+Z+P_x)^2-
\sum_{j=1}^r s_j(G+Z+P_0)^2
\right|=o_p(1). \tag{5}
\]
Applying the same block equations to the symmetric dilation and eliminating the strong coordinates leaves a Schur-complement error bounded by
\(C\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2/s_r(G)\).  Hence
\[
\sup_{|x|\leq M}
\left|s_{r+1}(G+Z+P_x)-s_1(Z_{22}+P_x)\right|=o_p(1). \tag{6}
\]

We next upgrade the cited pointwise outlier limit to the compact family needed here.  For a compact collection of deterministic two-by-two perturbations, choose a finite Frobenius \(\epsilon\)-net.  The singular-value variational formula gives
\[
|s_1(Z_{22}+P)-s_1(Z_{22}+\widetilde P)|
\leq\|P-\widetilde P\|_F. \tag{7}
\]
The noise operator norm is tight, and the two branches of \(\psi_\rho(s)\) agree at
\(s=\rho^{1/4}\); consequently \((\rho,s)\mapsto\psi_\rho(s)\) is continuous there.  The finite net, (7), and then \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) make the cited convergence uniform over this compact family.  When \(c>1\), apply the cited result to
\(c^{-1/2}(Z_{22}+P_x)^{\top}\), whose limiting aspect ratio is \(1/c\), and multiply the squared limit by \(c\).  This gives in both aspect regimes
\[
\psi_c(s)=
\begin{cases}
(1+\sqrt c)^2,&s\leq c^{1/4},\\
s^2+1+c+c/s^2,&s>c^{1/4}.
\end{cases} \tag{8}
\]
Replacing \((N,T)\) by \((N-r,T-r)\) and the entry variance \(1/(T-r)\) by \(1/T\) changes the limit by \(o(1)\).  A subsequence argument using the compact aspect envelope then yields
\[
\sup_{|x|\leq M}
\left|s_1(Z_{22}+P_x)^2-
\psi_{c_N}\{s_1(B_{NT,h}(x))\}\right|\xrightarrow{p}0. \tag{9}
\]

The Frobenius part is exact up to a scalar Gaussian term.  Orthogonality of \(P_x\) to the strong block gives
\[
\left\|\frac{Y-\beta D}{\sigma\sqrt T}\right\|_F^2
-\left\|\frac{Y-\gamma D}{\sigma\sqrt T}\right\|_F^2
=\|B_{NT,h}(x)\|_F^2-\|B_{NT,h}(0)\|_F^2
+2\langle Z,P_x-P_0\rangle_F. \tag{10}
\]
The final term is affine in \(x\), has mean zero, and has variance at most \(C_M/T\) uniformly on \(|x|\leq M\); its supremum is therefore \(o_p(1)\).  The full-profile identity, (5), (6), (9), and (10) prove the asserted compact-profile convergence.

It remains to exclude coefficient escape.  Put
\[
R=\kappa^2h^2(\mu_a^2+v_a)(\mu_b^2+v_b),
\qquad
d_0^2=\kappa^2h^2v_av_b,
\qquad
L_\infty=d_0^2-(1+c). \tag{11}
\]
At \(x=0\), the matrix \(B_{\eta,h}(0)\) has rank one and squared singular value \(R\).  Direct substitution in the two branches of \(\psi_c\) gives
\[
L_\infty-\Phi_{\eta,h}(0)
=
\begin{cases}
d_0^2+2\sqrt c-R,&R\leq\sqrt c,\\
d_0^2+c/R,&R>\sqrt c.
\end{cases} \tag{12}
\]
In the first case the gap is at least \(d_0^2+\sqrt c\); in the second it is positive.  Since \(c\) is bounded away from zero and \(R\) is bounded above on the maintained compact set, (12) has a common positive lower bound.

To identify the stochastic tail, write the lower block as \(-t e_1f_1^{\top}+A\), where
\(|t|=\kappa_{NT}|x|\) and \(A=P_0+Z_{22}\).  The eigenvalue equation for
\((-t e_1f_1^{\top}+A)(-t e_1f_1^{\top}+A)^{\top}\), expanded around the simple eigenvalue \(t^2\), gives
\[
s_1(-t e_1f_1^{\top}+A)^2
=t^2-2t e_1^{\top}Af_1+\|A^{\top}e_1\|_2^2
+\|(I-e_1e_1^{\top})Af_1\|_2^2+O_p(|t|^{-1}). \tag{13}
\]
The remainder is uniform after \(|t|\) exceeds a fixed constant because \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_p(1)\).  Gaussian quadratic laws give limits \(1\) and \(c\) for the two noise quadratic terms, and all noise--spike cross terms vanish.  After cancellation with the Frobenius expression (10), the remaining deterministic term is
\[
\|(I-e_1e_1^{\top})P_0(I-f_1f_1^{\top})\|_F^2-(1+c)
=d_0^2-(1+c)=L_\infty. \tag{14}
\]
If \(|x|\) is comparable with \(\sqrt m\), apply the same finite-rank expansion jointly to the \(r\) strong baseline directions and the treatment direction.  The exact left and right orthogonality assumptions make these deterministic directions orthogonal before noise is added, and the same cancellations yield (14).  Thus every feasible sequence with \(|x_{NT}|\to\infty\) has normalized profiled criterion converging to the tail value in (14).  By (12), such a sequence cannot be globally minimizing.  A compactness and subsequence contradiction therefore supplies a common finite \(M_0\) for which all random global minimizers lie in \([-M_0,M_0]\) with probability tending to one.  This proves uniform \(O_p(1)\) localization.

On \([-M_0,M_0]\), compact-profile convergence applies.  The global profile singleton theorem gives a continuous unique minimizer and a positive separation outside every fixed neighborhood, uniformly on compact parameter sets.  Since \(\eta_{NT}\to\eta\), the same uniform continuity gives
\[
\sup\operatorname{dist}\{\mathcal S_{NT}(h),x_\star(\eta,h)\}\longrightarrow0. \tag{15}
\]
If either asserted argmin conclusion failed, the deterministic separation outside an \(\epsilon\)-neighborhood would remain positive while the stochastic criterion error tends uniformly to zero, an immediate contradiction.  This proves both distance convergence and
\(\widehat x_F-x_\star(\eta,h)\xrightarrow{p}0\).  Finally, the global singleton theorem applies to every
\((\eta,h)\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times\mathbb R\); hence the bounded experiment contains no genuine tie.

The target and normalized coefficient definitions give the exact finite-array identity
\[
\frac{\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})}{\sigma}
=\widehat x_F-h\mu_{a,N}\mu_{b,T}. \tag{16}
\]
The uniform profile theorem gives
\(\widehat x_F-x_\star(\eta,h)\xrightarrow{p}0\) uniformly on compact subsets of the bounded experiment.  The two moment assumptions give
\(\mu_{a,N}\mu_{b,T}\to\mu_a\mu_b\).  Substitution in (16) proves the asserted stochastic absorption law.

It remains to identify the phase exactly.  At the ATT coordinate
\(x_{\operatorname{ATT}}=h\mu_a\mu_b\), direct substitution in the two-by-two profile gives
\[
B_{\eta,h}(x_{\operatorname{ATT}})
=\kappa h
\begin{pmatrix}
0&\mu_a\sqrt{v_b}\\
\sqrt{v_a}\mu_b&\sqrt{v_av_b}
\end{pmatrix}. \tag{17}
\]
Sign changes of rows and columns are orthogonal transformations.  Therefore, with \(C_\eta\) from the absorption-phase definition,
\[
s_1\{B_{\eta,h}(x_{\operatorname{ATT}})\}
=\kappa|h|s_1(C_\eta). \tag{18}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\), \(\kappa>0\), \(v_a,v_b>0\), and
\(|\mu_a|,|\mu_b|>0\); thus \(s_1(C_\eta)>0\), so division in the definition of \(h_{\mathrm{crit}}\) is valid.

In the rotated scalar coordinates of the global singleton theorem, the point \(z=0\) is exactly
\(x=x_{\operatorname{ATT}}\), and its \(\tau(0)\) is the squared largest singular value in (18).  The theorem selects \(z_\star=0\) exactly when
\(\tau(0)^2\leq c\).  By (18), this condition is
\[
\kappa^4h^4s_1(C_\eta)^4\leq c
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
|h|\leq\frac{c^{1/4}}{\kappa s_1(C_\eta)}
=h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta). \tag{19}
\]
This includes \(h=0\) and equality at the spectral edge.  If the inequality is strict in the opposite direction, the global singleton theorem gives
\(0<z_\star<z_0\) and
\[
x_\star=\frac{\operatorname{sgn}(h\mu_a\mu_b)}{\kappa}(z_0-z_\star),
\qquad
h\mu_a\mu_b
=\frac{\operatorname{sgn}(h\mu_a\mu_b)}{\kappa}z_0. \tag{20}
\]
The two strict signed inequalities in the statement follow immediately from (20).

All entries of \(C_\eta\), the largest-singular-value map, \(c^{1/4}\), and \(\kappa\) are continuous on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\); the denominator in (19) is bounded away from zero there.  Hence \(h_{\mathrm{crit}}\) is continuous and positive.  The strict inverse image defining \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\) is therefore relatively open.  Compactness of \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\) implies that
\(h_{\mathrm{crit}}\) attains its minimum.  If \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\neq\varnothing\), its defining inequality gives
\(\overline h>\min_\eta h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\).  Conversely, if this strict inequality holds, take a minimizing \(\eta_0\) and choose
\(|h|\in(h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta_0),\overline h]\); then
\((\eta_0,h)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\).  This proves the claimed equivalence without adding a signal-reach assumption.

Fix a compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\).  By the exact phase theorem, every point in \(\mathcal K\) is strictly supercritical and
\(\widehat x_F\to x_\star\) uniformly.  In the sign-rotated two-by-two representation used by the global singleton theorem, the selected coordinate satisfies
\(0<z_\star<z_0\), while the other three matrix entries are strictly positive.  The off-diagonal entry of the corresponding two-by-two left Gram matrix is therefore strictly positive.  Its two eigenvalues are distinct, so \(s_\star\) is simple.  Equation (19) and the strict supercritical selection rule also give \(s_\star>c^{1/4}\).  Compactness supplies uniform gaps both from the spectral edge and from the second population singular value.

Let \(e_1,f_1\) be the treatment-support vectors in (2).  The strong-block equations (1)--(6), evaluated at \(\widehat x_F\), show that the first \(r\) selected left and right singular spaces converge to \(U_0\) and \(V_0\).  The additional selected singular pair is the leading outlier pair generated by
\(Z_{22}+P_{x_\star}\), because replacing \(\widehat x_F\) by \(x_\star\) changes the perturbation by \(o_p(1)\) in operator norm.  For \(c\leq1\), the cited singular-vector-overlap theorem gives
\[
|\langle\widehat u,e_1\rangle|^2
\xrightarrow{p}\ell_c(s_\star)u_{\star,1}^2,
\qquad
|\langle\widehat v,f_1\rangle|^2
\xrightarrow{p}r_c(s_\star)v_{\star,1}^2. \tag{21}
\]
The factors \(u_{\star,1}^2\) and \(v_{\star,1}^2\) appear because the cited theorem also makes projections on the distinct population singular-vector direction vanish.  When \(c>1\), apply that theorem to
\(c^{-1/2}(Z_{22}+P_{x_\star})^{\top}\).  Its aspect ratio is \(1/c\), its spike is \(s_\star/\sqrt c\), and its left and right vectors are interchanged.  Algebra gives
\[
\frac{s_\star^4/c^2-1/c}
{(s_\star^2/c)(s_\star^2/c+1/c)}
=\frac{s_\star^4-c}{s_\star^2(s_\star^2+1)}=r_c(s_\star),
\]
\[
\frac{s_\star^4/c^2-1/c}
{(s_\star^2/c)(s_\star^2/c+1)}
=\frac{s_\star^4-c}{s_\star^2(s_\star^2+c)}=\ell_c(s_\star),
\]
so (21) holds for every \(c>0\).  Edge and simplicity separation make the convergence uniform on \(\mathcal K\).

Since \(D=\sqrt{n_1t_1}\,e_1f_1^{\top}\), and since
\(e_1\perp U_0\) and \(f_1\perp V_0\),
\[
\frac{\|\widetilde D\|_F}{\sqrt{NT}}
=\sqrt{p_Nq_T}\,
\|(I-P_{\widehat U})e_1\|_2
\|(I-P_{\widehat V})f_1\|_2. \tag{22}
\]
Substitution of (21) into (22), followed by \(p_N\to p\) and \(q_T\to q\), proves the displayed formula for \(a_D\).  For every finite
\(s>c^{1/4}\), direct subtraction from one gives
\[
0<\ell_c(s)<1,
\qquad
0<r_c(s)<1. \tag{23}
\]
Thus both factors defining \(a_D\) are strictly positive even when a first population singular-vector coordinate has absolute value one.  Continuity and compactness give a common positive lower bound on \(\mathcal K\).

We next prove variance consistency.  The absorption law gives
\(\widehat\beta_F-\gamma=O_p(m^{-1/2})\).  With
\[
R_{NT}=H-(\widehat\beta_F-\gamma)D,
\]
the bounded-score assumptions, the aspect envelope, and the share envelope give
\(\operatorname{rank}(R_{NT})\leq2\) and \(\|R_{NT}\|_F=O_p(\sqrt T)\).  Choosing
\(L=\Lambda F^{\top}\), which has rank at most \(r+1\), in the profiled residual problem yields
\[
\|Y-\widehat\beta_FD-\widehat L_F\|_F^2
\leq\|E+R_{NT}\|_F^2
=\|E\|_F^2+o_p(NT), \tag{24}
\]
where the last step follows from
\(2\|E\|_F\|R_{NT}\|_F+\|R_{NT}\|_F^2=o_p(NT)\).

For the reverse bound, write
\[
Y-\widehat\beta_FD-\widehat L_F=E-K_{NT},
\qquad
K_{NT}=\widehat L_F-(\Lambda F^{\top}+R_{NT}).
\]
Then \(\operatorname{rank}(K_{NT})\leq2r+3\).  The singular-value variational characterization of best fixed-rank approximation therefore gives
\[
\|Y-\widehat\beta_FD-\widehat L_F\|_F^2
\geq\|E\|_F^2-\sum_{j=1}^{2r+3}s_j(E)^2. \tag{25}
\]
The Gaussian law of large numbers and the Gaussian operator-norm bound imply
\[
\frac{\|E\|_F^2}{NT}\xrightarrow{p}\sigma^2,
\qquad
\frac1{NT}\sum_{j=1}^{2r+3}s_j(E)^2
=O_p(N^{-1})=o_p(1). \tag{26}
\]
Equations (24)--(26) show that the residual sum of squares divided by \(NT\) converges to \(\sigma^2\).  Since \(r\) is fixed and the aspect ratio is bounded away from zero and infinity,
\(\nu_F/(NT)\to1\); the nonnegative-root convention then gives
\(\widehat\sigma_F\xrightarrow{p}\sigma\), uniformly on \(\mathcal K\).

Finally define
\[
b(\eta,h)=x_\star(\eta,h)-h\mu_a\mu_b.
\]
The exact phase classification makes \(b\) continuous and nonzero on
\(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\), so \(\inf_{\mathcal K}|b|>0\).  The absorption law gives
\[
\frac{\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})}{\sigma}
\xrightarrow{p}b(\eta,h), \tag{27}
\]
whereas (22), variance consistency, and \(NT\asymp m^2\) give
\[
\frac{\sqrt m}{\sigma}
\frac{z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_F}{\|\widetilde D\|_F}
=O_p(m^{-1/2})\longrightarrow0. \tag{28}
\]
If the Wald interval contains the target, the absolute value on the left of (27) cannot exceed (28).  The positive uniform lower bound for \(|b|\) makes the probability of that event tend to zero uniformly on \(\mathcal K\).  The relative openness and the exact nonemptiness criterion for
\(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\) were proved in the absorption theorem, completing the result.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Suppose \(\eta_{NT}\to\eta\).  Uniformly over compact subsets of
\(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times[-\overline h,\overline h]\) and every finite \(M\),
\[
\sup_{|x|\leq M}\left|
\frac{Q_F(\gamma+\sigma x/\sqrt m)-Q_F(\gamma)}{\sigma^2T}
-\{\Phi_{NT,h}(x)-\Phi_{NT,h}(0)\}
\right|\xrightarrow{p}0.
\]
Moreover, \(\widehat x_F=O_p(1)\) uniformly,
\[
\operatorname{dist}\{\widehat x_F,\mathcal S_{NT}(h)\}\xrightarrow{p}0,
\qquad
\widehat x_F-x_\star(\eta,h)\xrightarrow{p}0
\]
uniformly on those compact sets.  Here \(h=\theta/\sigma\).  The global singleton theorem implies
\(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}=\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times[-\overline h,\overline h]\),
so no genuine limiting tie occurs anywhere in the bounded experiment.  No stochastic assertion is made for \(|h|>\overline h\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The proved global singleton result makes the former genuine-tie caveat empty.  The replacement writes the bounded domain explicitly as \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times[-\overline h,\overline h]\), retains both original localization conclusions, and records the resulting direct convergence to the unique minimizer without changing any assumption.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Uniformly over every compact subset of
\(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times[-\overline h,\overline h]\),
\[
\frac{\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})}{\sigma}
\xrightarrow{p}x_\star(\eta,h)-h\mu_a\mu_b.
\]
The exact phase classification is
\[
x_\star(\eta,h)=h\mu_a\mu_b
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
|h|\leq h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta).
\]
If \(|h|>h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\), then the minimizer lies strictly between zero and the ATT coordinate in its signed direction:
\[
0<x_\star(\eta,h)<h\mu_a\mu_b
\quad\text{when }h\mu_a\mu_b>0,
\]
and
\[
h\mu_a\mu_b<x_\star(\eta,h)<0
\quad\text{when }h\mu_a\mu_b<0.
\]
The set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\) is relatively open in
\(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times[-\overline h,\overline h]\), and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\neq\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\overline h>\min_{\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta).
\]
No assertion is made for \(|h|>\overline h\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current unconditional claim that an absorbed subset is nonempty is false when the bounded signal range does not reach the rectangular edge.  The replacement gives the exact same-assumption threshold, qualifies nonemptiness by the necessary-and-sufficient reach condition, and removes the now-impossible tie caveat.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
At \((\eta,h)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\), put
\[
B_\star=B_{\eta,h}\{x_\star(\eta,h)\},
\qquad s_\star=s_1(B_\star),
\]
and let \(u_\star,v_\star\in\mathbb R^2\) be unit left and right singular vectors for \(s_\star\), with first coordinates \(u_{\star,1}\) and \(v_{\star,1}\).  The top singular value is simple and \(s_\star>c^{1/4}\).  Define
\[
\ell_c(s)=\frac{s^4-c}{s^2(s^2+c)},
\qquad
r_c(s)=\frac{s^4-c}{s^2(s^2+1)},
\]
and
\[
a_D(\eta,h)=\sqrt{pq}
\left\{1-\ell_c(s_\star)u_{\star,1}^2\right\}^{1/2}
\left\{1-r_c(s_\star)v_{\star,1}^2\right\}^{1/2}>0.
\]
For every compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\), uniformly over \((\eta,h)\in\mathcal K\),
\[
\frac{\|\widetilde D\|_F}{\sqrt{NT}}\xrightarrow{p}a_D(\eta,h),
\qquad
\widehat\sigma_F\xrightarrow{p}\sigma,
\qquad
\Pr\{\operatorname{ATT}_{NT}\in\mathrm{CI}_F\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus conventional full-sample IFE Wald coverage is strictly below \(1-\alpha\), indeed asymptotically zero, throughout compact subsets of the absorption phase.  This phase is relatively open and is nonempty exactly when
\[
\overline h>\min_{\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta).
\]
All conclusions concern only the bounded experiment \(h=\theta/\sigma\in[-\overline h,\overline h]\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current theorem incorrectly asserts an unconditionally nonempty failure region.  The replacement restricts the conclusion to compact subsets of the exact absorption phase, states the necessary-and-sufficient nonemptiness criterion, and exposes the singular-vector-overlap formula for the residual design.

proposed.name: Exact rectangular detectability and absorption phase
proposed.construction:
For \(\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\), set
\[
C_\eta=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&|\mu_a|\sqrt{v_b}\\
|\mu_b|\sqrt{v_a}&\sqrt{v_av_b}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)
=\frac{c^{1/4}}{\kappa s_1(C_\eta)}.
\]
The denominator is positive on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\).  Define the bounded-experiment absorption phase by
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}
=\left\{(\eta,h)\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times[-\overline h,\overline h]:
|h|>h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\right\}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: This construction names the explicit edge threshold and the bounded-experiment phase consumed by the two delivered theorems.

\[
\sup_{|x|\leq M}\left|
\frac{Q_F(\gamma+\sigma x/\sqrt m)-Q_F(\gamma)}{\sigma^2T}

\]
Moreover, \(\widehat x_F=O_p(1)\) uniformly,

\]

proposed.justification: This is the bridge from fixed-spike random-matrix theory to the coefficient selected by the actual full-sample IFE objective throughout the bounded local experiment.
proposed.gap: Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi (2012) give fixed-spike limits; Bai (2009) does not provide uniform coefficient-indexed spectral localization or the global scalar selection used here.
proposed.consumer: It supplies uniform localization and direct convergence to the unique scalar-profile minimizer needed by the exact absorption phase and Wald-failure results.

proposed.statement:
Uniformly over every compact subset of
\(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times[-\overline h,\overline h]\),
\[
\frac{\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})}{\sigma}
\xrightarrow{p}x_\star(\eta,h)-h\mu_a\mu_b.
\]
The exact phase classification is
\[
x_\star(\eta,h)=h\mu_a\mu_b
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
|h|\leq h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta).
\]
If \(|h|>h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\), then the minimizer lies strictly between zero and the ATT coordinate in its signed direction:
\[
0<x_\star(\eta,h)<h\mu_a\mu_b
\quad\text{when }h\mu_a\mu_b>0,
\]
and
\[
h\mu_a\mu_b<x_\star(\eta,h)<0
\quad\text{when }h\mu_a\mu_b<0.
\]
The set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\) is relatively open in
\(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times[-\overline h,\overline h]\), and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\neq\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\overline h>\min_{\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta).
\]
No assertion is made for \(|h|>\overline h\).
proposed.justification: This theorem gives the exact bounded-local ATT-absorption phase law, including the critical selection and the reach condition for a nonempty absorbed region.
proposed.gap: Cardoso, Ferman, and Fernandes (2026) give a strong-signal endpoint; they do not give this noise-scale rectangular detectability threshold or its globally selected transition map.
proposed.consumer: The law tells a full-sample Bai-IFE analysis exactly when local treatment-supported heterogeneity is left in the coefficient and when it is partially absorbed by the fitted factor.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The false unconditional nonemptiness clause must be replaced by the exact phase threshold and its necessary-and-sufficient reach condition.

proposed.statement:
At \((\eta,h)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\), put
\[
B_\star=B_{\eta,h}\{x_\star(\eta,h)\},
\qquad s_\star=s_1(B_\star),
\]
and let \(u_\star,v_\star\in\mathbb R^2\) be unit left and right singular vectors for \(s_\star\), with first coordinates \(u_{\star,1}\) and \(v_{\star,1}\).  The top singular value is simple and \(s_\star>c^{1/4}\).  Define
\[
\ell_c(s)=\frac{s^4-c}{s^2(s^2+c)},
\qquad
r_c(s)=\frac{s^4-c}{s^2(s^2+1)},
\]
and
\[
a_D(\eta,h)=\sqrt{pq}
\left\{1-\ell_c(s_\star)u_{\star,1}^2\right\}^{1/2}
\left\{1-r_c(s_\star)v_{\star,1}^2\right\}^{1/2}>0.
\]
For every compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\), uniformly over \((\eta,h)\in\mathcal K\),
\[
\frac{\|\widetilde D\|_F}{\sqrt{NT}}\xrightarrow{p}a_D(\eta,h),
\qquad
\widehat\sigma_F\xrightarrow{p}\sigma,
\qquad
\Pr\{\operatorname{ATT}_{NT}\in\mathrm{CI}_F\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus conventional full-sample IFE Wald coverage is strictly below \(1-\alpha\), indeed asymptotically zero, throughout compact subsets of the absorption phase.  This phase is relatively open and is nonempty exactly when
\[
\overline h>\min_{\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta).
\]
All conclusions concern only the bounded experiment \(h=\theta/\sigma\in[-\overline h,\overline h]\).
proposed.justification: On the exact supercritical phase, the selected-factor bias has order \(m^{-1/2}\) while the explicitly residualized conventional interval has order \(m^{-1}\).
proposed.gap: Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026) establish possible weak-factor distortion but not this explicit overlap formula and zero-coverage phase for a rank-one block treatment.
proposed.consumer: For the Gobillon--Magnac full-sample Bai-IFE workflow, the result converts the exact detectability threshold into a certified conventional-Wald failure region whenever the bounded experiment reaches that threshold.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The Wald theorem must use the exact absorbed set, expose the residual-design overlap formula, and repeat the same nonemptiness criterion.

prose_updates.tldr: This paper studies an abstract exact-oracle panel experiment in which four finite-array orthogonality restrictions remove ordinary baseline confounding without fixing the profiled coefficient.  The full-sample IFE coefficient has a uniformly localized two-by-two spiked-SVD profile with an always-separated singleton minimizer.  It equals the ATT coordinate exactly when \(|h|\le h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\), and beyond that threshold it moves strictly toward the common effect.  The absorbed phase is relatively open and is nonempty exactly when \(\overline h>\min_{\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\); on its compact subsets the conventional residualized IFE Wald interval has asymptotically zero coverage.  Masked fitting remains an internal benchmark control.

project_justification.gap: Existing panel theory covers regular strong factors, generic weak-factor robustness, or a strong bad-control endpoint, while rectangular random-matrix theory fixes the spike before taking limits.  It does not supply the globally selected coefficient-indexed phase boundary \(h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\) after baseline-confounding terms are removed by defining restrictions.
project_justification.niche: An exact-oracle noise-scale treatment factor creates a nonregular but fully classifiable transition: ATT is retained through the spectral edge and is partially absorbed strictly beyond it.
project_justification.fill: The project derives \(\Phi_{\eta,h}\), proves uniform bounded-local profile convergence and an always-separated singleton minimizer, identifies \(h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)=c^{1/4}/[\kappa s_1(C_\eta)]\), proves that the absorbed phase is nonempty exactly under the stated reach inequality, and derives the explicit residual-design overlap and conventional-Wald zero-coverage law there.

prose_updates.related_work: Bai (2009) supplies the regular profiled-IFE and strong-factor framework, but not a coefficient-indexed noise-scale treatment spike.  Moon and Weidner (2015) study harmless rank overestimation under conditions excluding this low-rank regressor geometry.  Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi (2012) supply the fixed-spike rectangular outlier and singular-vector-overlap maps; this paper embeds those maps in the global coefficient profile and proves that the ATT coordinate is selected exactly through \(|h|=h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\).  Bloemendal and Virag (2013) study near-edge laws, whereas the critical point here remains a unique first-order selection.  Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026) motivate weak-factor-robust inference but exclude the rank-one block treatment through non-collinearity.  Cardoso, Ferman, and Fernandes (2026) establish the strong treatment-factor bad-control endpoint, not the bounded local phase or its exact reach condition.  Bai and Ng (2021) motivate observed-block imputation, and Gobillon and Magnac (2016) motivate comparing whole-sample and counterfactual factor fits; the present exact-oracle result is a sensitivity benchmark rather than a direct empirical identification claim.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The four exact orthogonality restrictions define the admissible triangular-array class.  They eliminate baseline-factor cross terms and isolate absorption by the fitted singular direction, but they are not observable residualization conditions.  Within this class the scalar profile has an always-separated singleton, including at \(|h|=h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\).  An absorbed region exists in the bounded experiment only when \(\overline h>\min_{\eta}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\); no signal-reach assumption is imposed to force that inequality.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proposal is an abstract exact-oracle sensitivity benchmark.  All stochastic profile, selection, absorption, and Wald conclusions concern \(\theta\in[-K,K]\) and \(h=\theta/\sigma\in[-\overline h,\overline h]\).  There is no genuine tie in this domain: the coefficient equals the ATT coordinate at and below the explicit threshold and lies strictly between the ATT coordinate and zero above it.  The absorbed phase may be empty, and it is nonempty exactly when \(\overline h>\min_{\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\).  Exact finite-array orthogonality is a defining restriction, not an observable procedure.  Masked fitting is only an internal control, not a claimed new practical estimator, and no stochastic conclusion is extended to unbounded \(|h|\).

statement_notes.justification: This theorem links the actual full-sample IFE objective to the explicit two-by-two profile and, using global singleton separation, localizes the selected coefficient uniformly throughout the bounded experiment.
statement_notes.gap: Fixed-spike random-matrix limits do not themselves control a coefficient-indexed global argmin.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies direct convergence to the unique profile minimizer for the exact phase and Wald calculations.

statement_notes.justification: This is the exact local ATT-absorption phase law, including the critical selection and the necessary-and-sufficient reach condition for nonemptiness.
statement_notes.gap: The strong-signal endpoint does not identify the bounded rectangular threshold or the selected transition path.
statement_notes.consumer: It tells the full-sample enterprise-zone IFE workflow exactly when treatment-supported heterogeneity remains in the coefficient and when fitted factors absorb part of it.

statement_notes.justification: Strictly beyond the same threshold, the order-\(m^{-1/2}\) absorption bias dominates an order-\(m^{-1}\) conventional standard error.
statement_notes.gap: Generic weak-factor results do not provide this rank-one treatment overlap formula or its exact nonempty phase.
statement_notes.consumer: It converts the phase law into uniform zero coverage for conventional full-sample IFE Wald inference on every compact absorbed subregion.

proofs.proof_tex:
Because \(\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\), the coordinates \(c,p,q,v_a,v_b\) are strictly positive, \(\mu_a\mu_b\neq0\), and
\[
 \kappa=\sqrt{\max\{c,1\}pq}>0.
\]
First suppose \(h\neq0\), and define the orthogonal sign matrices
\[
 U=\operatorname{diag}\{\operatorname{sgn}(\mu_a),1\},
 \qquad
 V=\operatorname{diag}\{\operatorname{sgn}(h\mu_b),\operatorname{sgn}(h)\}.
\]
Writing \(s=\operatorname{sgn}(h\mu_a\mu_b)\), direct substitution in the definition of \(B_{\eta,h}(x)\) gives
\[
 UB_{\eta,h}(x)V
 =\begin{pmatrix}z&b_0\\c_0&d_0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad z=z_0-s\kappa x,
\]
where
\[
 z_0=\kappa|h\mu_a\mu_b|,
 \quad b_0=\kappa|h\mu_a|\sqrt{v_b},
 \quad c_0=\kappa|h\mu_b|\sqrt{v_a},
 \quad d_0=\kappa|h|\sqrt{v_av_b}.
\]
All of \(b_0,c_0,d_0,z_0\) are strictly positive, and
\[
 \frac{b_0c_0}{d_0}=z_0.
\]
Left and right multiplication by orthogonal matrices preserves the Frobenius norm and every singular value.  Moreover, \(x\mapsto z_0-s\kappa x\) is a bijection of \(\mathbb R\).  Thus \(\Phi_{\eta,h}(x)\) is exactly the scalar criterion in \(\text{lem:scalar-profile-singleton}\), with \(\rho=c\), under this affine change of coordinate.  That lemma proves that the unique global minimizer is \(z_\star=0\) when \(\tau(0)^2\le c\), and otherwise is the unique \(z_\star\in(0,z_0)\) satisfying \(\mathcal R(z_\star)=c\).  Inverting the affine change gives
\[
 x_\star(\eta,h)=\frac{s}{\kappa}(z_0-z_\star).
\]
Since \(sz_0/\kappa=h\mu_a\mu_b\), this also shows that the minimizer equals \(h\mu_a\mu_b\) in the first case and lies strictly between \(0\) and \(h\mu_a\mu_b\), in the signed direction, in the second case.

If \(h=0\), then \(B_{\eta,0}(x)=-\kappa xe_{11}\).  When \(\kappa^2x^2\le\sqrt c\), the definition of \(\psi_c\) yields
\[
 \Phi_{\eta,0}(x)=\kappa^2x^2-(1+\sqrt c)^2,
\]
whose unique minimum on this region is attained at \(x=0\).  When \(\kappa^2x^2>\sqrt c\), it yields
\[
 \Phi_{\eta,0}(x)=-(1+c)-\frac{c}{\kappa^2x^2}
 >-(1+\sqrt c)^2=\Phi_{\eta,0}(0).
\]
Hence \(x_\star(\eta,0)=0\), uniquely.

We next prove continuity and the uniform separation assertion.  The map \((\eta,h,x)\mapsto\Phi_{\eta,h}(x)\) is continuous: the entries of \(B_{\eta,h}(x)\) are continuous, singular values are continuous functions of the entries, and the two branches defining \(\psi_c\) agree when \(s=c^{1/4}\).  Consequently, the profiles converge uniformly on bounded \(x\)-sets whenever their parameters converge.

It remains to control the tails uniformly.  Let \(\lambda_1(\eta,h,x)\ge\lambda_2(\eta,h,x)\ge0\) be the two squared singular values of \(B_{\eta,h}(x)\), and put
\[
 d_0^2=\kappa^2h^2v_av_b,
 \qquad
 S=\kappa^2h^2(\mu_a^2+v_a)(\mu_b^2+v_b).
\]
The rank-one identity for \(A_\eta\) gives
\[
 \det B_{\eta,h}(x)=-\kappa^2xh\sqrt{v_av_b}.
\]
The quadratic formula for \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\), together with the fact that \(\kappa\) is bounded away from zero on compact subsets of \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\), therefore gives, uniformly on every compact parameter set,
\[
 \lambda_1(\eta,h,x)\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad
 \lambda_2(\eta,h,x)longrightarrow d_0^2
 \quad\text{as }|x|\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Indeed, the squared Frobenius norm is \(\kappa^2x^2+O(|x|+1)\), uniformly on such a set, while
\(\lambda_1\lambda_2=\kappa^4x^2h^2v_av_b\).  The outlier branch of \(\psi_c\) hence implies the uniform tail limit
\[
 \Phi_{\eta,h}(x)\longrightarrow d_0^2-(1+c).
 \tag{1}
\]
At \(x=0\), the matrix \(B_{\eta,h}(0)=\kappa hA_\eta\) has rank at most one and its nonzero squared singular value is \(S\).  Subtracting \(\Phi_{\eta,h}(0)\) from the limit in (1) gives
\[
 G(\eta,h)=
 \begin{cases}
 d_0^2+2\sqrt c-S,&S\le\sqrt c,\\
 d_0^2+c/S,&S>\sqrt c.
 \end{cases}
\]
This function is continuous across \(S=\sqrt c\) and strictly positive.  In fact, on the first branch \(G\ge d_0^2+\sqrt c>0\), and on the second branch positivity is immediate.  Thus, on every compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times\mathbb R\), continuity gives \(\inf_{\mathcal K}G>0\).  The uniform convergence in (1) then supplies an \(M<\infty\) and a \(g>0\) such that, for every \((\eta,h)\in\mathcal K\) and \(|x|>M\),
\[
 \Phi_{\eta,h}(x)\ge\Phi_{\eta,h}(0)+g.
 \tag{2}
\]
In particular, all global minimizers over \(\mathcal K\) belong to one common bounded interval.

Now let \((\eta_n,h_n)\to(\eta,h)\) and write \(x_n=x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\).  Apply (2) to the compact set consisting of this sequence and its limit.  Every subsequence of \((x_n)\) has a further convergent subsequence.  If its limit is \(\bar x\), local uniform convergence of the profiles and the inequalities
\[
 \Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}(x_n)\le\Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}(y),\qquad y\in\mathbb R,
\]
show that \(\Phi_{\eta,h}(\bar x)\le\Phi_{\eta,h}(y)\) for every fixed \(y\).  The uniqueness already proved forces \(\bar x=x_\star(\eta,h)\).  Hence the entire sequence converges, proving continuity of \((\eta,h)\mapsto x_\star(\eta,h)\), including at \(h=0\) and at the spectral boundary.

Fix a compact \(\mathcal K\) and \(\varepsilon>0\).  If the uniform separation in (8) failed, there would be \((\eta_n,h_n)\in\mathcal K\) and \(x_n\) with
\[
 |x_n-x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)|\ge\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 \Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}(x_n)-
 \Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}\{x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{3}
\]
If \((x_n)\) is bounded, compactness, continuity of \(x_\star\), and local uniform convergence produce a limiting point distinct from the unique limiting minimizer but having the same criterion value, a contradiction.  If \((x_n)\) is unbounded along a subsequence, (2) and
\(\Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}\{x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\}\le\Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}(0)\) bound the difference in (3) below by \(g>0\), again a contradiction.  This proves (8), and in particular every parameter point belongs to \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{stab}}\).

For the stated stochastic consequence, let \(\varepsilon>0\) and use (8) to denote the corresponding uniform deterministic gap by \(g_\varepsilon>0\).  Uniform tightness permits choosing \(M\) so that \(\widehat x_n\in[-M,M]\) with probability tending to one; enlarge \(M\) so that all \(x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\) also lie in that interval.  On the event that the displayed centered criterion approximation in the theorem is smaller than \(g_\varepsilon/2\) uniformly on \([-M,M]\), no point in that interval at distance at least \(\varepsilon\) from \(x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\) can have criterion value no larger than the value at \(x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\).  Since \(\widehat x_n\) is a global minimizer, it follows that
\[
 \Pr\{|\widehat x_n-x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)|\ge\varepsilon\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus a next-order selector is unnecessary.

Finally, fix a critical point with \(h\neq0\) and \(\tau(0)^2=c\).  We first verify the derivative sign used in the expansion.  At \(z=0\), let \(t=\tau(0)\), let \(u\) be the smaller squared singular value of \(M(0)\), and let \(w=z_0\).  Then
\[
 t+u=Q(0),\qquad tu=d_0^2w^2,
\]
and the nonzero off-diagonal entry of \(M(0)^{\top}M(0)\) makes \(t>u>0\).  Differentiating
\[
 \tau(z)^2-Q(z)\tau(z)+d_0^2w(z)^2=0
\]
at zero, using \(Q'(0)=0\) and \(w'(0)=-1\), yields
\[
 \tau'(0)=\frac{2d_0^2w}{t-u}.
\]
Since \(\mathcal R(0)=t^2\), logarithmic differentiation of the displayed formula for \(\mathcal R\) gives
\[
 \frac{\mathcal R'(0)}{\mathcal R(0)}
 =\frac{2\tau'(0)}t+\frac wt-\frac{t}{d_0^2w}
 =\frac{4u}{w(t-u)}-\frac{w(t-u)}{tu}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Furthermore,
\[
 M(0)^{\top}M(0)
 =\begin{pmatrix}c_0^2&c_0d_0\\c_0d_0&b_0^2+d_0^2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its smaller eigenvalue satisfies \(u<c_0^2\), since the Rayleigh quotient at the first coordinate vector is \(c_0^2\) and that vector is not an eigenvector because \(c_0d_0>0\).  Hence
\[
 (t-u)^2-4d_0^2u
 =(c_0^2-b_0^2-d_0^2)^2+4d_0^2(c_0^2-u)>0.
\]
Using \(tu=d_0^2w^2\), this strict inequality is equivalent to the right-hand side of (4) being negative.  Therefore \(\mathcal R'_0(0)<0\).

Consider now an admissible path converging to this critical point and satisfying
\(\Delta_\epsilon=\tau_\epsilon(0)^2-c_\epsilon
=\epsilon\dot\Delta+o(\epsilon)\).  The identity
\[
 \mathcal R_\epsilon(0)-c_\epsilon=\Delta_\epsilon
\]
and the exact selection rule show that \(z_{\star,\epsilon}=0\) whenever \(\Delta_\epsilon\le0\).  Whenever \(\Delta_\epsilon>0\), the selected root obeys
\[
 0=\mathcal R_\epsilon(z_{\star,\epsilon})-c_\epsilon.
\]
Continuity of the minimizer, already proved, gives \(z_{\star,\epsilon}\to0\).  The mean-value theorem and continuity of \(\mathcal R_\epsilon'\) near zero therefore yield
\[
 z_{\star,\epsilon}
 =\epsilon\frac{(\dot\Delta)_+}{-\mathcal R'_0(0)}+o(\epsilon).
\]
Because the limiting \(h\), \(\mu_a\), and \(\mu_b\) are nonzero, \(s_\epsilon=s\) for all sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), while \(\kappa_\epsilon\to\kappa\).  The exact inverse-coordinate identity
\[
 x_{\star,\epsilon}-h_\epsilon\mu_{a,\epsilon}\mu_{b,\epsilon}
 =-\frac{s_\epsilon}{\kappa_\epsilon}z_{\star,\epsilon}
\]
then proves the asserted second expansion.  In particular, taking \(\epsilon=m^{-1/4}\) changes only a term that vanishes without this additional rescaling.  Opposite local drifts can therefore change the directional derivative but, by continuity and uniqueness, cannot yield distinct separated limiting selections at the same limiting nuisance coordinates.
